about.title: National City Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: San Diego County recorded 6 traffic deaths in National City in the most recent final crash year, alongside 296 injury collisions and 412 people hurt. Behind each of those numbers is a family trying to make sense of a sudden loss, often after a crash along Highland Avenue, E Plaza Boulevard, National City Boulevard, or the I-5 corridor. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to bring a wrongful death claim. If no one in that first group survives, other dependents or heirs may have standing. These cases are separate from any criminal charges that might follow a fatal crash, and they exist to help families recover funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's guidance and companionship. LawProactive doesn't practice law directly, but we can connect grieving families in National City with an independent attorney who can explain these rights and next steps, at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: What Families in National City Should Know

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines Apply
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity involve a much shorter notice period. Missing these windows can end a family's right to recover, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: Standing to bring a wrongful death claim goes first to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children; if none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify. An independent attorney can help sort out who has the legal right to bring the claim.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, but also compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. These non-economic losses are real and recognized by law.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in National City?
items.answer: California generally sets a two-year deadline from the date of death for wrongful death claims. If the crash involved a government vehicle or a city-maintained road, a much shorter notice deadline may apply, sometimes just months. Speaking with an independent attorney early helps make sure no deadline is missed.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file the claim?
items.answer: California law puts a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children first in line to bring a wrongful death claim. If none of those relatives survive, other dependents or heirs may have standing instead. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to clarify who qualifies.

items.question: Does National City's crash data affect our case?
items.answer: Public crash records showing where and when collisions happen, such as the pattern of crashes near Highland Avenue or during Wednesday evening rush hour, can sometimes provide helpful context for a case. They don't determine outcomes, but an attorney may use this kind of record alongside other evidence when reviewing what happened.

items.question: What kinds of losses can our family recover?
items.answer: California allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses and the financial support your loved one would have provided. Families may also seek compensation for the loss of that person's love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can walk you through how these categories might apply to your circumstances.
